11: /// ## What it does
12: /// Checks for unnecessary dictionary unpacking operators (`**`).
13: ///
14: /// ## Why is this bad?
15: /// Unpacking a dictionary into another dictionary is redundant. The unpacking
16: /// operator can be removed, making the code more readable.
17: ///
18: /// ## Example
19: /// ```python
20: /// foo = {"A": 1, "B": 2}
21: /// bar = {**foo, **{"C": 3}}
22: /// ```
23: ///
24: /// Use instead:
25: /// ```python
26: /// foo = {"A": 1, "B": 2}
27: /// bar = {**foo, "C": 3}
28: /// ```
29: ///
30: /// ## References
31: /// - [Python documentation: Dictionary displays](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#dictionary-displays)
32: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
33: pub(crate) struct UnnecessarySpread;
34: 
35: impl Violation for UnnecessarySpread {
36:     const FIX_AVAILABILITY: FixAvailability = FixAvailability::Sometimes;
37: 
38:     #[derive_message_formats]
39:     fn message(&self) -> String {
40:         "Unnecessary spread `**`".to_string()
41:     }
42: 
43:     fn fix_title(&self) -> Option<String> {
44:         Some("Remove unnecessary dict".to_string())
45:     }
46: }

48: /// PIE800
49: pub(crate) fn unnecessary_spread(checker: &mut Checker, dict: &ast::ExprDict) {
50:     // The first "end" is the start of the dictionary, immediately following the open bracket.
51:     let mut prev_end = dict.start() + TextSize::from(1);
52:     for ast::DictItem { key, value } in dict {
53:         if key.is_none() {
54:             // We only care about when the key is None which indicates a spread `**`
55:             // inside a dict.
56:             if let Expr::Dict(inner) = value {
57:                 let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(UnnecessarySpread, value.range());
58:                 if let Some(fix) = unnecessary_spread_fix(inner, prev_end, checker.locator()) {
59:                     diagnostic.set_fix(fix);
60:                 }
61:                 checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
62:             }
63:         }
64:         prev_end = value.end();
65:     }
66: }

68: /// Generate a [`Fix`] to remove an unnecessary dictionary spread.
69: fn unnecessary_spread_fix(
70:     dict: &ast::ExprDict,
71:     prev_end: TextSize,
72:     locator: &Locator,
73: ) -> Option<Fix> {
74:     let source = locator.contents();
75:     let source_len = locator.text_len();
76:     let search_start = locator.floor_char_boundary(prev_end);
77:     if source.is_empty() {
78:         return None;
79:     }
80: 
81:     let dict_start = dict.start();
82: 
83:     let mut doublestar: Option<SimpleToken> = None;
84:     for tok in SimpleTokenizer::starts_at(search_start, source) {
85:         if tok.end() <= source_len {
86:             if tok.kind() == SimpleTokenKind::DoubleStar {
87:                 if !tok.range().is_empty() && !locator.contains_line_break(tok.range()) {
88:                     doublestar = Some(tok);
89:                     break;
90:                 }
91:             }
92:         }
93:     }
94: 
95:     let doublestar = doublestar?;
96:     if doublestar.start() > dict_start {
97:         return None;
98:     }
99: 
100:     // Determine whether the dictionary is wrapped in parentheses. The
101:     // parentheses have to be removed along with the `**` operator, otherwise
102:     // the fix would introduce a syntax error.
103:     // Ex) `**({"a": 1})`
104:     let mut leading_parens = 0usize;
105:     let mut leading_lparens = Vec::new();
106:     if doublestar.end() < dict_start {
107:         for tok in SimpleTokenizer::starts_at(doublestar.end(), source) {
108:             if tok.start() >= dict_start {
109:                 break;
110:             }
111:             match tok.kind() {
112:                 SimpleTokenKind::LParen => leading_lparens.push(tok),
113:                 kind if kind.is_trivia() => {}

115:                 // unexpected; bail out of the fix.
116:                 _ => return None,
117:             }
118:         }
119:         leading_parens = leading_lparens.len();
120:     }

122:     // Collect the closing parentheses that match the leading parentheses.
123:     let mut trailing_rparens: Vec<SimpleToken> = Vec::new();
124:     if leading_parens > 0 {
125:         if let Some(last) = dict.iter_values().last() {
126:             let trailing_start = last.end();
127:             let mut seen_rbrace = false;
128:             for tok in SimpleTokenizer::starts_at(trailing_start, source).skip_trivia() {
129:                 if !seen_rbrace && tok.start() >= dict.end() {
130:                     // We've scanned past the closing brace of the dictionary
131:                     // without seeing it; bail out.
132:                     break;
133:                 }
134:                 match tok.kind() {
135:                     SimpleTokenKind::RBrace => {
136:                         seen_rbrace = true;
137:                     }
138:                     SimpleTokenKind::RParen if seen_rbrace => {
139:                         trailing_rparens.push(tok);
140:                         if trailing_rparens.len() == leading_parens {
141:                             break;
142:                         }
143:                     }
144:                     // Skip any other tokens before the closing brace (e.g., a
145:                     // trailing comma, or the closing parenthesis of a
146:                     // parenthesized value like `(a := 1)` whose range does not
147:                     // include the parentheses).
148:                     _ if !seen_rbrace => {}
149:                     // Stop at any unexpected token after the closing brace.
150:                     _ => break,
151:                 }
152:             }
153:         } else {
154:             for tok in SimpleTokenizer::starts_at(dict.end(), source).skip_trivia() {
155:                 match tok.kind() {
156:                     SimpleTokenKind::RParen => {
157:                         trailing_rparens.push(tok);
158:                         if trailing_rparens.len() == leading_parens {
159:                             break;
160:                         }
161:                     }
162:                     _ => break,
163:                 }
164:             }
165:         }
166:         if trailing_rparens.len() != leading_parens {
167:             return None;
168:         }
169:     }
170: 
171:     if let Some(last) = dict.iter_values().last() {
172:         // Ex) `**{a: 1, b: 2}` or `**(  # Comment
173:         //                         {a: 1, b: 2}  # Comment
174:         //                     )`
175:         let mut edits = vec![Edit::range_deletion(doublestar.range())];
176:         if leading_parens > 0 {

178:                 leading_lparens

189:             match tok.kind() {
190:                 SimpleTokenKind::Comma => {
191:                     edits.push(Edit::range_deletion(tok.range()));
192:                 }
193:                 SimpleTokenKind::RBrace => {
194:                     edits.push(Edit::range_deletion(tok.range()));
195:                     break;
196:                 }
197:                 _ => {}
198:             }
199:         }
200:         edits.extend(
201:             trailing_rparens
202:                 .iter()
203:                 .map(|tok| Edit::range_deletion(tok.range())),
204:         );
205:         Some(Fix::safe_edits(edits.remove(0), edits))
206:     } else {

208:         let mut edits = vec![Edit::range_deletion(doublestar.range())];
209:         if leading_parens > 0 {

211:                 leading_lparens
212:                     .iter()
213:                     .map(|tok| Edit::range_deletion(tok.range())),
214:             );
215:             edits.push(Edit::deletion(dict.start(), dict.end()));
216:             edits.extend(
217:                 trailing_rparens

223:             Some(Fix::safe_edit(Edit::deletion(
224:                 doublestar.start(),
225:                 dict.end(),
226:             )))

Fixed. The bug was in `unnecessary_spread_fix` in crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/flake8_pie/rules/unnecessary_spread.rs:69 — the PIE800 fix deleted `**{` but ignored parentheses wrapping the spread dict (e.g. `**({"count": ...})`), leaving unbalanced `(` `)` behind.

The rewritten fix generation now:
- Detects leading `(`s between `**` and the dict's `{` (bailing out on anything unexpected)
- Emits separate deletions for the `**`, each leading `(`, the `{`, any comma before the dict's `}`, the `}`, and the matching trailing `)`s — preserving comments and whitespace
- Skips stray tokens (trailing commas, the closing paren of a parenthesized value like `(a := 1)`) between the last value and the dict's `}` before collecting the matching closers
- Handles the empty-dict case (`**({})`) as well

- `cargo test -p ruff_linter --lib`: all 2220 tests pass, including the PIE800 snapshot test with its parenthesized/comment/nested-paren/walrus fixtures
- clippy and fmt clean
